:::{#exm-mutual-information-noisy-copy}
#### Mutual information of a noisy copy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X$ be a fair coin toss, coded $0$ or $1$.
Let $Y$ equal $X$ with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.8$ and the other value with probability $0.2$.
The [joint distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-distribution) gives probability $0.4$ to $(0, 0)$ and $(1, 1)$ and $0.1$ to $(0, 1)$ and $(1, 0)$.
The chunk computes the [mutual information](#def-mutual-information) in [bits](#def-bit)
from the divergence formula in @thm-mutual-information-kl.

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
joint <- matrix(
  data = c(0.4, 0.1, 0.1, 0.4),
  nrow = 2,
  dimnames = list(x = 0:1, y = 0:1)
)
p_x <- rowSums(joint)
p_y <- colSums(joint)
product <- outer(X = p_x, Y = p_y)
terms <- joint * log2(joint / product)
mutual_information <- sum(terms)
mutual_information
```

So $\mutinfof{X}{Y} = `r round(mutual_information, 3)`$ bits.
This matches $\entropyf{Y} - \entropyf{Y \mid X}$,
which is $1$ [bit](#def-bit) minus the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) of a coin with probabilities $0.8$ and $0.2$.
That is $1 - `r round(-0.8 * log2(0.8) - 0.2 * log2(0.2), 3)`$ bits.

:::
